jobs.title: Payment Operations Manager
jobs.description:
At Cardless, we’re building a credit card and loyalty platform that consumer businesses use to engage their customers. We’ve launched 14 credit cards, including for Coinbase, Alibaba, and Qatar Airways. We help businesses bring imaginative card programs to life, and have pioneered technology to embed credit card features natively into their products.

We value curiosity, humility, and intensity — we move fast and take ownership. This is a place where a motivated, resourceful individual can have an enormous impact on our trajectory. We're headquartered in San Francisco, and have raised about $90M in equity funding from top venture capital firms and angels.



The Job

We’re hiring a Payments Operations Manager to scale and operate the infrastructure behind Cardless’s card programs.

This individual contributor role sits at the center of our payments ecosystem. Working with our key operational systems, managing external partners (processors, issuing banks, networks), and driving high-impact initiatives like processor integrations, program launches, and process improvements.

You’ll balance hands-on operational execution with program-level ownership, ensuring our payments systems are reliable, scalable, and ready to support new products and partners. You’ll identify the highest-leverage opportunities to automate, build the tooling (or spec it for engineering), and make sure our ops team can support 10x the volume without 10x the headcount.



Before You Apply

A few things worth knowing:

 - This is an IC role. You won’t have direct reports. You’ll be a high performing individual contributor embedded in a small, high-output payment ops team. 

 - We work in the office 5 days a week. We know that’s a dealbreaker for some people, and that’s okay.

 - We move fast and operate with imperfect information. If you prefer fully defined problems and complete context before acting, this role may not be the right fit.

 - Fintech complexity is real. Credit cards sit at the intersection of product, compliance, fraud, and banking. You'll need to get fluent quickly and build that fluency into everything you create.

If that sounds like your kind of work, keep reading.



Impactful Role Scope & Responsibilities



You’ll work on programs people care about. Coinbase. Bilt. Qatar Airways. These aren’t test programs. They’re products with real cardholders and real transaction volume.

 - Reimagine how we onboard and operate. You will own the automation of the card lifecycle workflows end-to-end by spotting manual pain points, designing smarter solutions, and partnering with Engineering to bring them to life.

 - Get close to the product and build cards people love, improving operations and strengthening partnerships to make great credit card experiences possible.



This role is about scale. Drive the scale of Cardless payment operations by building processes and systems that handle growing complexity and volume seamlessly as we expand to millions of cardholders.

 - Working directly in the payment operations world and analyzing tickets to uncover root causes and drive fixes that solve underlying problems, not just surface issues.

 - Operationalizing network mandates. Build intake and tracking processes, assessing impact, and coordinating implementation across Ops and Engineering to ensure nothing falls through the cracks.

 - Support the BPO and back-office operations strategy—scaling external partnerships while establishing SOPs, training and audit frameworks to ensure quality and consistency.



You’ll be on the frontier of AI and automation in payments. Exception handling, reconciliation and monitoring are some of the highest-leverage areas in fintech today, and you’ll be building those systems, not watching from the sidelines.

 - Build internal ops dashboards. Scope and deliver a unified view of card production, transaction exceptions, inventory levels and processor health—giving the team real-time visibility without relying on Engineering.

 - Leverage AI to design and evolve processes, SOPs, and tooling to eliminate manual work while improving reliability, and enabling real-time monitoring and reporting.



Requirements

 - 5+ years in payment or card operations (issuer, processor, or fintech)

 - Experience with card processors, reconciliation, and network file formats (Visa, Mastercard, Amex)

 - Strong SQL and comfort using data to diagnose issues and validate solutions

 - Experience building or improving operational tooling and automation

 - Knowledge of network mandates, BINs, and card lifecycle operations

 - Clear communicator across teams

 - Comfortable in fast-moving, ambiguous environments; fintech experience is a plus



Compensation

The expected cash compensation for this role is $150,000–$180,000 annually, plus equity and benefits. Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skills, experience, and specific work location.



Benefits

We’re proud to offer our team excellent benefits:



💸  Meaningful startup equity

🏥  100% health, vision & dental primary coverage

➕  75% health, vision & dental dependent coverage

🍱  Catered lunches

🚎  $250/month commuter benefit

👶  Parental leave

✈️  Team building events & happy hours

🌴  Flexible PTO with a minimum of 15 days off per year

🖥️  Apple equipment

💸  401k plan



Location

We’re headquartered in San Francisco, CA. This role is in-office 5 days a week.

jobs.title: Fraud Strategy Manager / Senior Manager (Onboarding)
jobs.description:
At Cardless, we’re building a credit card and loyalty platform that consumer businesses use to engage their customers. We’ve launched 14 credit cards, including for Coinbase, Alibaba, and Qatar Airways. We help businesses bring imaginative card programs to life, and have pioneered technology to embed credit card features natively into their products.

We value curiosity, humility, and intensity — we move fast and take ownership. This is a place where a motivated, resourceful individual can have an enormous impact on our trajectory. We're headquartered in San Francisco, and have raised about $90M in equity funding from top venture capital firms and angels.




THE JOB

We're looking for a Fraud Strategy Manager or Senior Manager – Onboarding to own the end-to-end fraud strategy for how we evaluate new applicants. This is a highly analytical, strategy-forward role focused on building the decisioning framework that determines which applicants are approved, stepped up for review, or declined, and making sure the tools, data, and processes behind those decisions are best-in-class.



Reporting to our Chief Risk Officer, you'll work at the intersection of data, tooling, and operations to sharpen our onboarding defenses as Cardless scales in the next year. You'll own the manual review program, drive the strategy for leveraging alternative data signals from bank data, device intelligence, and partner sources, and build the measurement infrastructure to continuously improve performance.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN



Manual Review Strategy & Operations

 - Define the logic and thresholds for routing applicants into manual review, balancing fraud risk against approval rates and customer experience.

 - Own the manual review program end-to-end: queue prioritization, SLA design, analyst tooling, and case escalation paths.

 - Evaluate the effectiveness of tools used in manual review; identify gaps and advocate for new capabilities that help analysts make faster, higher-quality decisions.

 - Track manual review outcomes rigorously: analyst decisions, approval/decline rates, reversal rates, downstream fraud on reviewed accounts, and false positive costs.

 - Build structured feedback loops between review outcomes and upstream rules triggers to drive continuous policy refinement.



Alternative Data & Signal Development

 - Lead the strategy for incorporating bank account data into onboarding decisions, leveraging signals such as account tenure, balance history, income patterns, and return/NSF activity.

 - Operationalize device intelligence and behavioral signals to strengthen identity and fraud detection at the top of the funnel.

 - Develop a framework for using partner data: loyalty engagement, transaction history, tenure signals as supplementary fraud indicators in co-brand card programs.

 - Evaluate new data sources and vendors on an ongoing basis; build a rigorous test-and-learn methodology to validate signal lift before production deployment.



Fraud Detection & Rules Ownership

 - Own the fraud rules framework for onboarding: design, test, implement, and continuously tune rules across identity, velocity, device, funding, and behavioral dimensions.

 - Partner with data science to define feature requirements, evaluate model performance, and translate model outputs into operational policy.

 - Document all policy decisions clearly, including the tradeoffs made at each threshold.



Performance Measurement & Portfolio Monitoring

 - Define and own the KPI framework for onboarding fraud: fraud rate by vintage and partner, manual review rate, auto-decisioned bad rate, tool efficacy, and cost-per-review.

 - Conduct regular portfolio reviews to surface emerging fraud patterns, track loss trends, and assess detection performance.

 - Build reporting to enable real-time monitoring, trend identification, and rapid policy response.



Cross-Functional Partnership

 - Partner with Product and Engineering to translate fraud strategy into system requirements and influence roadmap prioritization.

 - Work with Compliance and Legal to ensure onboarding controls meet BSA/AML, Red Flags Rule, ECOA, and UDAAP requirements.

 - Collaborate with Customer Operations to manage edge cases, decision appeals, and applicant escalations.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5–10 years of experience in fraud strategy, identity risk, or credit risk at a financial institution, fintech, or payments company.

 - Deep expertise in onboarding fraud — synthetic identities, identity manipulation, first-party fraud vectors, and deposit/funding fraud.

 - Hands-on experience with bank data providers in a fraud or credit risk context.

 - Familiarity with device intelligence and behavioral fraud platforms.

 - Strong SQL skills and experience using data to build and evaluate fraud rules, track performance, and identify emerging patterns.

 - Excellent communication skills — you can translate complex fraud tradeoffs into clear recommendations for executives, partners, and compliance teams.

 - Proactive, bias-to-action mindset: you ask the right questions, align stakeholders, and drive decisions forward.




COMPENSATION

This role has an annual starting salary range of $150,000 - $210,000 + equity + benefits (see below). Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors, including but not limited to skills, experience, and specific work location.




BENEFITS

We're headquartered in San Francisco, CA, with a beautiful office in the Mission District. We're proud to offer our team excellent benefits:

💸 Meaningful Start-up equity

🏥 100% health, vision & dental primary coverage

➕ 75% health, vision & dental dependent coverage

🍱 Catered lunches

🚎 $250/month Commuter benefit

👶 Parental leave

✈️ Team building events & happy hours

🌴 Flexible PTO with a minimum of 15 days off per year

🖥️ Apple equipment

💸 401k plan




LOCATION

We're headquartered in San Francisco, CA, with a beautiful office in the Financial District. We welcome employees who want to work from this office; we offer additional benefits to those who do, and relocation assistance to those who'd like to.

We regularly bring our team together for offsites & trips, about every 2 months, both for fun and for work. We cover all travel & lodging in these cases.

jobs.title: Business Operations Associate
jobs.description:
ABOUT CARDLESS

Cardless is a Series C consumer fintech that makes it easy for the world’s largest brands to build credit cards into their ecosystems. Think Shopify, but for credit cards. Brands use Cardless to configure, launch, and grow credit card programs that delight their customers and strengthen their core business.

Customers include Coinbase, Bilt Rewards, Alibaba, Qatar Airways, and LATAM Airlines. Cardless powers cards on all three major networks (Visa, Mastercard, and American Express) and uses AI-powered servicing to operate at a fraction of the headcount traditional card issuers require.

Cardless raised a $60 million Series C led by Spark Capital in September 2025, bringing total funding past $170 million. The team is past 50 people and scaling toward profitability by year-end 2026.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Cardless is a fast-moving company where high-stakes conversations happen constantly — with partners, investors, and the board. This role exists to make sure those conversations land well. You will be the person who turns a rough idea into a polished deck, a meeting agenda into a tight follow-up, and a pile of data into a clear story.

As a BizOps Associate, you will work directly with Michael Spelfogel (President) to support the execution of day-to-day operations, prepare materials for key external meetings, and keep cross-functional work moving. This is not a strategy role — it is an execution role. The thinking happens at the top; your job is to make sure it is communicated clearly, tracked rigorously, and followed through.

You will be well-suited for this role if you came up through consulting or investment banking, know how to build a 10-slide deck that actually gets read, and want to apply those skills in a high-growth operating environment where the work is real and the stakes are high.




WHAT YOU WILL DO


BUILD DECKS AND MEETING MATERIALS

 - Own the production of presentation materials for partner meetings, quarterly business reviews, board meetings, and investor updates — from first draft to final polish.

 - Translate rough inputs — notes from a call, a verbal briefing, a half-finished slide — into clean, structured decks with a clear narrative arc.

 - Work directly with go to market team to prepare for high-visibility external conversations. Understand the audience, anticipate the questions, and make sure the materials are airtight before anyone walks in the room.

 - Maintain and iterate on recurring materials — partner-facing templates, internal scorecards, QBR frameworks — so they stay current and consistent.


SUPPORT OPERATING CADENCE

 - Prepare agendas, pre-reads, and follow-up materials for recurring meetings: leadership syncs, cross-functional reviews, and partner QBRs.

 - Track action items, decisions, and open questions across workstreams. Close the loop by ensuring commitments are documented and followed through.

 - Own the logistics and preparation behind key internal planning moments, including quarterly strategy reviews and annual planning.


SYNTHESIZE AND COMMUNICATE

 - Compile partner feedback, meeting notes, and cross-functional inputs into clear written summaries that help leadership make faster, better-informed decisions.

 - Draft memos, one-pagers, and briefing documents for internal and external use. Write with precision: no buried lede, no filler, no ambiguity.

 - Distill complex business situations into the two or three things that actually matter, and present them in a form that drives alignment rather than debate.




WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR


EXPERIENCE

 - 3–5 years of professional experience, with a strong preference for backgrounds in management consulting or investment banking. Operations, finance are also relevant.

 - A track record of building presentation materials that get used, not just delivered — you know what a good slide looks like, and you know the difference between a deck that informs and one that persuades.

 - Experience supporting senior leaders in high-stakes settings: preparing them for important meetings, managing follow-through, and keeping complex work organized.

 - Exposure to financial services or fintech is a plus, but not required. Intellectual curiosity about the space is required.


SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES

 - Deck-Building and Visual Storytelling: You know how to structure a narrative, make a slide scannable, and build a deck that moves an audience through a decision. You have strong instincts for what belongs and what doesn’t.

 - Written Communication: You write with clarity and economy. Your memos and summaries don’t need editing. You can take a complex situation and reduce it to its essential elements without losing nuance.

 - Structured Execution: You bring order to ambiguity. You can take a meeting that ends without resolution and convert it into a clear next step. You are organized, dependable, and accountable.

 - Analytical Thinking: You are comfortable pulling numbers together, identifying what matters, and presenting data in a way that makes the takeaway obvious. You don’t need to be a data scientist, but you can’t be afraid of a spreadsheet.

 - Low Ego, High Output: You care about the work, not the credit. You are happy to be the person behind the scenes making things run. You don’t need to own the strategy; you need to make sure it gets executed.

 - Discretion: You handle sensitive information with maturity. You work closely with leadership and will have visibility into things that are not for broader circulation.
   
   


THIS ROLE IS NOT A FIT IF

 - You are primarily looking for a strategy role with ownership over direction and roadmap — this role supports and enables that work; it does not own it.

 - You view slide-building and meeting preparation as beneath you — that work is core to this role, not incidental to it.

 - You need a highly defined scope and clear swim lane — this role requires comfort picking up whatever needs doing, even when it doesn’t fit neatly into a job description.

 - You require remote or hybrid work arrangements.




WHY THIS ROLE

Cardless is at an inflection point: the company has found product-market fit, raised the capital to scale, and is now executing against a clear roadmap to profitability. The work is consequential and the pace is fast.

This role offers direct exposure to the founders at a moment when the decisions being made will shape the next chapter of the company. If you came out of consulting or banking and want to apply those skills somewhere the stakes are real — not hypothetical — this is the right move.




COMPENSATION

This role has an annual starting salary range of $140,000–$175,000 + equity + benefits. Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skills, experience, and specific work location.

 


BENEFITS

We're proud to offer our team excellent benefits:

💸 Meaningful Start-up equity

🏥 100% health, vision & dental primary coverage

➕ 75% health, vision & dental dependent coverage

🍱 Catered lunches

🚎 $250/month Commuter benefit

👶 Parental leave

✈️ Team building events & happy hours

🌴 Flexible PTO with a minimum of 15 days off per year

🖥️ Apple equipment

💸 401k plan

 


LOCATION

We're headquartered in San Francisco, CA, with a beautiful office in Jackson Square. This role is in-office 5 days a week.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Bank Partnerships
jobs.description:
ABOUT CARDLESS

Cardless is building the infrastructure for the world's best companies to design, build, and launch financial products of their own. Companies like Coinbase and Bilt use Cardless to create credit cards that feel entirely their own. In an industry where branded financial products usually mean shared logos and shared control, Cardless is built to disappear. Our APIs and components shape the journey from the first application to every purchase, reward, and moment of support that follows, while we handle lending, compliance, and operations behind the scenes.

In September 2025, we raised a $60 million Series C led by Spark Capital, bringing our total funding to $170 million. The team is over 70 people and scaling toward profitability by year-end 2026.

We're looking for kind, humble people with high standards and low egos. We take the work seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. We see what could be improved, make it so, and leave every product, system, and team better than we found it.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a program manager to own the day-to-day working relationship between Cardless and the banks that issue our cards, and to run new card programs from signed deal to live launch. You will be our bank partners' primary point of contact, the person who knows where every open item stands and keeps each partner informed early. Cardless is a program manager that partners with FDIC- and OCC-regulated issuing banks to design and deliver co-branded credit cards, so the work has to account for obligations across multiple bank partners with different regulators, expectations, and reporting cadences. Understanding that structure, where the bank holds the regulatory obligation and we perform the work, is key to succeeding here.

This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role with no direct reports. You sit on the Compliance team and report to our Chief Compliance Officer. As our portfolio grows, this role brings bank partner management into one seat: you will build the trackers, the reporting rhythm, and the governance cadence for it, and your first assignment is a live program launch.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the day-to-day relationship with our issuing bank partners as their primary point of contact for program status, open items, approvals, and escalations.

 - Personally write the documents our partners read: status packages, launch trackers with real dates behind them, diligence responses, and partner correspondence. You author the judgment in them, not just the formatting.

 - Communicate risks and timeline changes to bank partners accurately and early, and commit only to dates the delivery team has agreed to.

 - Run new program launches end to end: kickoff, the requirements and approvals checklist, partner-facing materials, legal and compliance milestones, and the launch timeline, coordinating Compliance, Legal, Product, Engineering, and Operations so each item arrives at the bank complete.

 - Build and run the governance cadence with each partner (recurring check-ins, steering committees, quarterly reviews) and maintain the obligations tracker for each bank agreement, keeping internal owners to their dates.

 - Translate internal workstreams into clear, partner-ready updates, prepare our team for partner meetings, and identify friction on rewards, payments, disputes, and other program mechanics early, routing it to the right owner with a proposed answer.

 - Support due diligence and onboarding for new bank and brand partners, and examination and audit requests that come through our bank partners, and use AI and automation tooling to keep trackers, status packages, and checklists current.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 10+ years in program management, partnerships, or account management at a bank, fintech, payments company, or other regulated financial services company. This is a requirement, not a preference: experience outside financial services does not qualify on its own.

 - You have personally sat across from a bank or a regulator as the person responsible for a program, a deliverable, or a response.

 - Demonstrated ability to manage complex, multi-stakeholder relationships where technical, legal, and business considerations all have to be balanced, working cross-functionally with compliance, legal, product, and engineering.

 - Strong writing. You can take a messy cross-functional situation and produce a clear, accurate, partner-ready document from a blank page.

 - A bias toward early communication. You would rather raise a risk now than have a partner learn of it late, and you can describe a time you did.

 - Comfort operating in ambiguity, building process where none exists yet, and using data and AI tools to work more efficiently.

 - You live within a reasonable commute of our San Francisco office, or you are relocating before you start (see the note on location below).

Bonus Points

 - Experience with card issuing, co-branded credit card programs, or working directly with issuing or sponsor banks, from either side of the relationship.

 - Familiarity with the regulatory considerations that shape bank and fintech partnerships: third-party risk management, program governance, and what an examination asks of a service provider.

 - Experience launching a new financial product from contract signing through go-live, or a technical program management background.


THIS ROLE ISN'T A FIT IF

 - We work in the office 5 days a week in San Francisco (Jackson Square), and that is our strong preference. If you are in the Bay Area and would need a hybrid schedule, or you are based in the Salt Lake City area, apply anyway and tell us in your application; we would rather have the conversation than miss you. If you need a fully remote role, this is not the seat.

 - There is no playbook for this role and no daily check-in. If you do your best work with structure handed to you, this is not the seat.

 - This is a hands-on build, not a maintenance job. If you are looking for a quiet role with settled processes, this is not the seat.

 - This seat writes the document, not the meeting invite about it. If you would rather coordinate the author than be the author, this is not the seat.


WHY THIS ROLE

You are the person who writes the document, not the person who schedules the meeting about it. You have delivered difficult news to a counterparty early because you understood that late news costs more than early news. You know that a bank partner is a supervised institution with obligations of its own, and you can reason from that to what needs to be escalated and how fast. You are comfortable with a blank page, and you build a mechanism rather than absorbing the work by hand.

 - Own the relationship with the banks that issue our cards, as the single voice they hear from first, reporting to our Chief Compliance Officer.

 - Run a live program launch as your first assignment, from signed deal to go-live, and build the trackers, reporting rhythm, and governance cadence that the next programs run on.

 - Sit at the intersection of Compliance, Legal, Product, Engineering, and Operations, with the bank partners on the other side of the table.

What success looks like at six months. Our bank partners hear about every material development from us first, the launch you inherited has gone live on the timeline you held, the governance cadence runs without our CCO needing to be in every meeting, and the reporting rhythm you built is the one a second and third program run on.


COMPENSATION

This role has an annual starting salary range of $150,000 to $200,000 plus equity and benefits (see below). Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skills, experience, and specific work location.


PERKS & BENEFITS

We're proud to offer our team excellent benefits:

 - 💸 Meaningful Start-up equity

 - 🏥 100% health, vision & dental primary coverage

 - ➕ 75% health, vision & dental dependent coverage

 - 🍱 Catered lunches

 - 🚎 $250/month Commuter benefit

 - 👶 Parental leave

 - ✈️ Team building events & happy hours

 - 🌴 Flexible PTO with a minimum of 15 days off per year

 - 🖥️ Apple equipment

 - 💸 401k plan

jobs.title: Chief of Staff, Office of the President
jobs.description:
ABOUT CARDLESS

Cardless is building the infrastructure for the world's best companies to design, build, and launch financial products of their own. Companies like Coinbase and Bilt use Cardless to create credit cards that feel entirely their own. In an industry where branded financial products usually mean shared logos and shared control, Cardless is built to disappear. Our APIs and components shape the journey from the first application to every purchase, reward, and moment of support that follows, while we handle lending, compliance, and operations behind the scenes.

In September 2025, we raised a $60 million Series C led by Spark Capital, bringing our total funding to $170 million. The team is over 70 people and scaling toward profitability by year-end 2026.

We're looking for kind, humble people with high standards and low egos. We take the work seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. We see what could be improved, make it so, and leave every product, system, and team better than we found it.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

You will work extremely closely with, and act as a force multiplier to the founder and president: taking on our hardest, most complex, most interdisciplinary problems… to make sure the company runs well and wins!!




YOU SHOULD EXPECT THE ROLE TO PROGRESS AS FOLLOWS:

 1. First day: Welcome to the team. 👋

 2. Shadowing: Shadow the founder to understand how the company works, and rapidly accumulate context on our business. You’ll join exec team meetings, external pitches, interviews, product workshops – travel to visit partners and customers, and go very very deep on the most important problems.

 3. Solve your first problem: You’ll eventually get bored and feel compelled to dive in and start solving problems. At this stage you take on your first problem and solve it. This could be anything across the business… rebuilding an operational or product process, designing a new product feature, creating a new business line, etc…

 4. Take on harder and harder problems: You’ll continue operating as a problem solver across the business, and as you become formidable, the problems will grow more complicated and more impactful. Over time, you may fall in love with a specific part of the company and move into it full-time, or help us launch a new business line, or even (if /when the time is right) leave to start a company!







WHY YOU SHOULD NOT JOIN:

 - This is an IC role – if you’re looking to manage large teams of people, this role is not for you. If you’re looking to become a very effective problem solver, and learn founder leadership skills, this could be the right place!

 - We plan to hire multiple CoS’in the company. If it’s important to you to be the only person in this role at the company, this role is not for you. However, we run our team lean, to ensure a very healthy opportunity: people ratio so opportunity will still abound!

 - We work very hard – long hours, often on weekends (often on Sundays but never on Saturdays). We understand that winning takes a level of intensity and dedication that others are simply unwilling to.

 - Wherever you are weak, this role will push you to grow. You will face unfamiliar problems that demand you learn quickly and improve continuously. Learning and growing is kind of painful, and this role expects you to lean into that discomfort, over and over again.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

 - Intellectual vitality, you are endlessly curious about how to build a great business, and more broadly, how the worlds of finance and technology work.

 - Extremely driven – motivated to build an amazing company and an incredible career, because you love seeing what you’re capable of.

 - 5+ years experience doing hard things: this could be through any of a wide range of experiences: consulting, banking, engineering, product, operating, founding a company, taking over a family business, etc…

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a compliance professional to own consumer complaints end to end and to turn complaint trends into fixes that address root causes, not just one-off resolutions. We see complaints as direct feedback from our most valued asset, our customers, and we treat that signal with the weight it deserves. You'll partner closely with our Customer Experience team on investigation and response, own trending and reporting to our bank partners, and take on the part most complaint roles never get to: tracing patterns back to root cause and driving the remediation that closes the loop. Cardless is a program manager that partners with FDIC- and OCC-regulated issuing banks, so your work has to meet the expectations of multiple bank partners, each with its own regulator, categorization standards, and reporting cadence.

This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role. You will personally work critical complaints, review responses, and work with Customer Experience and Engineering to fix underlying defects. We have a working complaint program and are investing in better tooling; you will own the program, lead the tooling implementation, and take it to its next stage.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own intake, triage, categorization, investigation, and resolution for consumer complaints across our card programs, including agency complaints from the CFPB, FDIC, Better Business Bureau, state attorneys general, and counsel.

 - Draft investigation summaries and consumer responses that are accurate, plain-spoken, and defensible if a regulator reads them later, and manage target dates so nothing is late.

 - Produce the monthly complaint reporting package for each bank partner, adapted to that partner's categorization and reporting expectations, and quarterly complaint findings for the Compliance Committee and the Board.

 - Analyze complaint volume, categories, and drivers to find patterns, and distinguish a one-time servicing error from a product defect, a disclosure gap, a broken workflow, or a control failure.

 - Convert confirmed root causes into logged issues with corrective action plans, owners, and target dates, then drive remediation to closure with Engineering, Product, and Operations and confirm the theme stops recurring.

 - Work side by side with Customer Experience to improve how complaints are identified, tagged, and documented at first contact, and write the procedures, response templates, and agent guidance that let the front line handle routine matters correctly.

 - Improve complaint tooling, intake workflows, and reporting, including automation, and keep records examination ready.

 - Provide coverage across other compliance functions as needed.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Typically 4 to 7 years in consumer compliance, complaint management, disputes, or a closely related function within banking, fintech, credit cards, lending, or payments, with hands-on experience investigating and resolving consumer and agency complaints.

 - Working knowledge of the regulations complaints turn on: Regulation Z, Regulation E, Regulation B, UDAAP, FCRA, and FDCPA.

 - Demonstrated root cause analysis skill: you can take a cluster of complaints, work out what is causing them, and say so in writing with evidence.

 - Experience driving corrective action across functions you do not manage, particularly Engineering and Operations, through to validated closure.

 - Excellent written communication, and comfort using data and AI tools to work more efficiently and expand coverage.

 - Organized and self-directed: many open matters with hard deadlines, no playbook, no daily check-in, and nothing gets dropped.

Bonus Points

 - Experience in credit card issuing or co-branded card programs, or responding to CFPB portal complaints alongside a partner bank.

 - Background in disputes, fraud, or servicing operations, where many complaint root causes live.

 - Experience building or maturing a complaint program, or writing procedures and agent guidance for a support organization.

 - CRCM or another consumer compliance certification.


THIS ROLE ISN'T A FIT IF

 - We work in the office 5 days a week in San Francisco. If you need a hybrid or remote schedule, this is not the seat.

 - There is no playbook for this role and no daily check-in. If you do your best work with structure handed to you, this is not the seat.

 - This is a hands-on build, not a maintenance job. If you are looking for a quiet compliance role with settled processes, this is not the seat.

 - Behind every complaint is a customer, and the job is to make the pattern stop. If the response letter is where your work ends, this is not the seat.


WHY THIS ROLE

 - You get the whole loop. Most complaint roles stop at the response letter. This one runs through root cause, corrective action, and validation, so you fix things rather than only respond to them.

 - Complaints are one of the most visible compliance functions we have. Your analysis goes to our bank partners, the Compliance Committee, and the Board, and you sit at the intersection of Compliance, Customer Experience, Engineering, and Product.

 - We are AI-forward. If you want to automate the repetitive parts of this job, we will give you the tools to do it.

What success looks like. In your first 90 days you own the complaint queue, every matter has a target date and is on track, and you have a first cut of categorization and trend reporting our bank partners recognize as an improvement. By six months you run a mature program: defined intake, consistent categorization, reliable monthly reporting to each bank partner, and quarterly findings to the Compliance Committee and the Board. You have taken at least two recurring complaint themes through root cause to validated remediation and the volume in those categories is measurably down. Customer Experience handles routine matters correctly at first contact because you gave them the procedures to do it, and complaints have become the early warning system the rest of the compliance program uses.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring someone to run compliance issue management at Cardless. That covers the issue log for all of our card programs, corrective action plans, consumer remediation, and monthly reporting to our bank partners. You'll take issues all the way to closed. That means the fix is actually in the product and you've checked it worked. The file should still make sense to an examiner a year later.

Cardless is a program manager. We partner with FDIC- and OCC-regulated issuing banks, each with its own regulator and reporting schedule, so most issues you work involve us, the brand partner and the bank.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with no direct reports, and we're open on level. Depending on your experience it could be an analyst or a manager title, and the offer will reflect that.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the compliance issue log across every card program and bank partner (intake, classification, root cause, target dates, status, closure) and keep it reconciled to each bank's register.

 - Document each issue: what happened, which requirement it touches, when it started, when customer impact ended, and how many customers were affected.

 - Write corrective action plans with an owner, a target date, and the evidence that will show the fix worked. If the permanent fix will take a while, put an interim control in place.

 - Work with Engineering, Product, and Operations on the underlying fix. An issue isn't closed until you've confirmed the fix held.

 - Scope affected populations, design the remediation, work with Finance and Operations to carry it out, then check afterward that each affected customer was made whole.

 - Send monthly issue reporting to each bank partner, answer partner and exam requests on open items, and prepare updates for the Compliance Committee and the Board.

 - Improve the tools and workflow behind all of this. Automate where it makes sense, and when the same kind of issue keeps coming up, add a control or monitoring to catch it earlier.

 - Help out in other compliance areas when needed.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You think critically. With incomplete information you can work out what happened, be upfront about what you're sure of and what you aren't, and explain why you scoped something the way you did. This matters more to us than anything else here.

 - You've personally taken a problem from "something looks off" to fixed and verified. It doesn't have to have been in compliance.

 - If you're coming in as a manager, you have working knowledge of Regulation Z, Regulation E, Regulation B, UDAAP, and FCRA from applying them. Analysts can learn them here, as long as the judgment is there.

 - You're comfortable with data and can tell whether a number is plausible. You use AI tools in your work now, and you check what they give you. You don't need to be an engineer.

 - Your writing is clear enough that a bank partner or regulator can follow it without a meeting.

 - You're organized. You can keep a lot of open items and deadlines moving on your own.

Bonus Points

 - SQL. If you can pull and check a population yourself, that's the most useful extra thing you could bring.

 - You've built your own tools, like scripts, automations, agents, or dashboards.

 - Background in consumer finance, cards, payments, disputes, or servicing, or experience with compliance issues, remediation, audit, or testing.

 - CRCM or another consumer compliance certification.


THIS ROLE ISN'T A FIT IF

 - You're looking for hybrid or remote. We're in our San Francisco office 5 days a week.

 - You prefer a defined playbook and regular check-ins. This role is pretty self-directed, and a lot of it is still being built.

 - You'd rather hand off once a fix ships. Part of this job is going back to confirm customers were taken care of.


WHY THIS ROLE

 - Leadership and our bank partners care about this work, and it goes to the Compliance Committee and the Board.

 - We're AI-forward and will give you the tools to automate the repetitive parts.

What success looks like. At 90 days you own the log, know every open item and who owns it, and your monthly reporting to each bank partner reconciles to their records. By six months intake and classification are consistent, corrective action plans have clear evidence standards, remediation is scoped by sub-issue and checked after payment, and our bank partners see the monthly reporting as an improvement. Issues you've closed stay closed, and recurring patterns have monitoring on them.


COMPENSATION

jobs.title: Director, Business Development
jobs.description:
ABOUT CARDLESS

Cardless is a Series C consumer fintech that uses AI to make it easy for the world's largest brands to build credit cards into their ecosystems. Think Shopify, but for credit cards. Brands use Cardless to configure, launch, and grow credit card programs that delight their customers and strengthen their core business.

Customers include Coinbase, Bilt Rewards, Alibaba, Qatar Airways, and LATAM Airlines. Cardless powers cards on all three major networks (Visa, Mastercard, and American Express) and uses agentic servicing to operate at a fraction of the headcount and cost that traditional card issuers require.

Cardless raised a $60 million Series C led by Spark Capital in September 2025, bringing total funding past $170 million. The team is past 70 people and scaling toward profitability by year-end 2026.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Cardless grows by landing new brand partners — and landing brand partners requires someone who can build relationships before there is a deal to discuss, navigate the processes that larger organizations use to make significant strategic decisions, and persuade companies that already have a card program that there is a better way to run one. This role is that person.

As Director of Business Development, you will own the top of the Cardless commercial funnel. You will identify the right prospects, build the relationships required to get in the room, and drive the process from first conversation through a signed term sheet. This role reports to the Chief Business Officer of Cardless.

This is a hands-on, individual contributor role with a clear mandate: Build an organized pipeline, bring brands closer to conversion, and negotiate durable and lucrative deals. You will be evaluated on the quality and velocity of the opportunities you generate and move forward.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

Build New Partner Relationships

 - Identify and prioritize the brands most likely to benefit from a Cardless card program — drawing on market data, competitive intelligence, and your own network to build a high-quality prospect list.

 - Develop relationships with senior decision-makers at target companies over the time horizon that enterprise deals require — not just the inbound conversations that happen to come in.

 - Represent Cardless credibly and compellingly to executives at major consumer brands, financial institutions, and loyalty programs — most of whom will already have opinions about the card space.

 - Work with Marketing and Product to ensure the materials, demos, and narratives you bring to market reflect what Cardless actually does and where it is going.

Work the Consulting and RFP Channel

 - Build and maintain relationships with the consulting firms and networks that run RFP and vendor selection processes for large card program decisions.

 - Ensure Cardless is known, understood, and credibly represented in the processes these firms run — which requires ongoing relationship maintenance, not just responding to RFPs as they arrive.

 - Develop a point of view on which consulting firms are most active in the card space, which relationships matter most, and where Cardless should invest relationship-building resources.

 - Respond to formal RFP processes with materials that are accurate, compelling, and differentiated — working with the product, finance, and partnerships teams to pull together the right inputs.

Target Companies with Existing Card Programs

 - Identify companies that currently have card programs through incumbent issuers — and build the case for why Cardless represents a materially better partner.

 - Develop deep familiarity with the competitive landscape: what the major incumbent issuers offer, where they fall short, and what a company that has lived through a card program launch actually cares about.

 - Build relationships at these companies in a way that is respectful of existing contracts and focused on what comes next — not adversarial to their current partners.

 - Work with the product and partnerships teams to ensure the Cardless pitch is grounded in real product capabilities and backed by the performance of existing programs.

Own the Business Development Process

 - Manage a pipeline of prospects from first contact through signed agreement, with the discipline and rigor that enterprise sales requires — accurate forecasting, clear next steps, and no deals falling through the cracks.

 - Work with the leadership team to prioritize which opportunities to pursue and at what pace, given the constraints of the partnerships team that will need to execute what BD signs.

 - Diligently maintain the systems — CRM, contact databases, outreach cadences — that make BD operations repeatable and scalable as the team grows.

 - Provide regular, honest reporting on pipeline health, deal velocity, and the competitive dynamics you observe in the market.
   
   


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Experience

 - 7-10 years in business development, partnerships, or a sales role with meaningful exposure to financial services — ideally including time at a bank, card issuer, or payment network.

 - A demonstrated track record of closing complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise deals — not just sourcing conversations, but owning the process from prospecting through signature.

 - Existing network in the card and payments space — relationships with decision-makers at consumer brands, financial institutions, loyalty programs, or the consulting firms that advise them.

 - Experience navigating formal RFP processes for financial services technology or infrastructure is a strong plus.

Skills and Competencies

 - Network and Relationship Building: You have spent years building relationships in the right places, and you know how to open a door that is not obviously open. Your network is a genuine competitive advantage, not a LinkedIn following.

 - Financial Services Fluency: You understand how card programs work — the economics, the players, the contract structures, the regulatory context — well enough to have a credible commercial conversation with a bank executive or a CFO.

 - Sales Process and Discipline: You run a clean pipeline. You know where every deal is, what the next step is, and what it will take to close it. You do not lose deals because something fell through the cracks.

 - Communication and Presence: You are effective in a room with senior executives. You can explain what Cardless does in two minutes and make it sound like the most obvious thing in the world. You can also write.

 - Competitive Intelligence: You stay current on what incumbents are doing, what new entrants are building, and how the market is evolving — and you use that knowledge to sharpen how Cardless is positioned.

 - Judgment and Autonomy: You can prioritize your own time across a large number of potential opportunities and make good calls about where to invest without needing to be managed at the activity level.
   
   


THIS ROLE IS NOT A FIT IF

 - Your background is primarily inbound sales or account management — this role requires the ability to generate cold pipeline through network and outbound effort, not manage relationships that someone else originated.

 - You do not have meaningful experience in financial services — a general enterprise sales background without exposure to banking, cards, or payments will not be sufficient for the conversations this role requires.

 - You are looking for a management role with a team to build — this is an individual contributor position, and the expectation is that you carry your own number before you hire under you.

 - You require remote or hybrid work arrangements.




WHY THIS ROLE

Cardless has found product-market fit, has live programs with major brands, and is growing fast. What it does not yet have is a dedicated business development function — the top of the commercial funnel has been driven by the founders and the CBO. This role is the first dedicated BD hire, which means the person who joins now will set the template for how Cardless does business development.

The strongest salespeople in financial services are typically selling products with a 30-year track record and a brand that opens doors for them. Cardless is asking for something harder: to sell a better version of a product that most of its prospects already have. If that challenge sounds more interesting than intimidating, this is the right role.
